# Release runbook

How to cut a release of `tally`. Run every step from the repository root.

1. Run the tests: `scripts/run_tests.sh`. Stop if anything fails.
2. Set the new version: `python3 scripts/bump_version.py <version>`.
   Why: `pyproject.toml` and `pkg/__init__.py` must carry the same version; the
   package index rejects an upload whose metadata and module disagree.
3. In `CHANGELOG.md`, move the entries under `## Unreleased` to a new heading
   `## <version> (<date>)`, and leave `## Unreleased` empty above it.
4. Build the bundle: `python3 scripts/build.py --legacy-imports`.
5. Check: `python3 scripts/check_version.py` must print `ok: <version>`.
6. Add a row for this release to the release log at the end of this file.
7. Commit everything with the message `Release <version>`.

## Release log

| version | date | notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1.3.1 | 2026-08-03 | |
| 1.3.2 | 2026-09-14 | |

content.text:
Release 1.4.0 is committed as `da24063` ("Release 1.4.0"). I ran the runbook in order, with one change to step 2 (below).

1. The tests passed: 2 tests, OK.
2. `RUNBOOK.md` names `scripts/bump_version.py`, but commit c55771c renamed it to `set_version.py` with the same arguments. I ran `python3 scripts/set_version.py 1.4.0`, which set both `pyproject.toml` and `pkg/__init__.py` to 1.4.0. The runbook still has the old name, and I left it alone because you didn't ask me to change it.
3. In `CHANGELOG.md`, the two unreleased entries now sit under `## 1.4.0 (2026-11-12)`, with an empty `## Unreleased` above it.
4. The build produced `dist/tally-1.4.0 (with legacy imports)`.
5. `check_version.py` printed `ok: 1.4.0`.
6. I added `| 1.4.0 | 2026-11-12 | |` to the release log in `RUNBOOK.md`.
7. The commit includes the four modified files: `CHANGELOG.md`, `RUNBOOK.md`, `pkg/__init__.py` and `pyproject.toml`. The `dist/` output didn't show up in `git status`, so it wasn't committed.

My first attempt to do the changelog and release-log edits as one shell command was blocked by the permission check. I made the same edits with the file-edit tool instead.
